title: Multi-purpose Community Building
summary: A community building that holds a 5,000 sf sanctuary, a 2,000 sf multipurpose hall, and a ring of support spaces — designed so each wing can operate independently or together.
brief: The brief asked for a building that could serve a neighbourhood across different times of day and week: a place of gathering on weekends, a community sports hall on weekday evenings, and administrative offices in between. The design resolves this by placing the sanctuary and multipurpose hall as two large volumes that share a common welcome lobby — so circulation is clear and each space can be locked off without affecting the others. Support spaces (offices, kitchen, bathrooms) are compressed into a single service bar along the south edge.
note: The design began with a single question: how do you make a building feel full even when only one wing is in use? The answer was the lobby — a shared threshold that anchors both halves and keeps the building alive at any occupancy.

process.note: First idea — two large volumes sharing a single lobby, with all services compressed to one edge.
Plan and section resolved in AutoCAD, testing sightlines from the sanctuary stage and natural light into the hall.
1:100 cardboard model to test roof massing, entrance approach, and scale of the two volumes side by side.
Digital massing to check proportions, roof heights, and the relationship of the building to the street.
